questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P. These gases have a profound effect on the earth despite making up only a fraction of all atmospheric gases.

Q. They are a contributor to the phenomenon known as the greenhouse effect.

R. Carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor are the most important greenhouse gases.

S. Greenhouse gases are gas molecules that absorb infrared radiation and reradiate it back.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**SQRP**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it begins with 'most' or 'once'.
 
• **Sentence S **will be the first sentence because it is an introductory sentence that tells us about** 'Greenhouse gases'.**
 
• **Sentence Q** will be used next because it further explains what the greenhouse effect contributes. 
 
• **Sentence R **will be the next sentence because it tells us about the most important greenhouse gases.
 
• Lastly,** Sentence P **will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
 
• **S**: Greenhouse gases are gas molecules that absorb infrared radiation and reradiate it back.
 
• **Q**: They are a contributor to the phenomenon known as the greenhouse effect.
 
• **R**: Carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor are the most important greenhouse gases.
 
• **P**: These gases have a profound effect on the earth despite making up only a fraction of all atmospheric gases.

 
 
 

**Correct Sequence:__** *Greenhouse gases are gas molecules that absorb infrared radiation and reradiate it back. They are a contributor to the phenomenon known as the greenhouse effect. Carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor are the most important greenhouse gases. These gases have a profound effect on the earth despite making up only a fraction of all atmospheric gases.*

questions.question:
Directions: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested below, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

**God helps the brave.**

options.text: The brave is helped by God.
The brave are helped by God.
The brave are help by God.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"The brave are helped by God."**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The provided sentence **"God helps the brave." **is in Active voice in the present simple tense.
 
• The structure of this active voice sentence can be described as follows: **"Subject (God) + Base form of verb (helps) + Object (the brave)."**
 
• To convert this sentence from active voice to passive voice, the positions of the subject and object are switched around, with the object moving to the start of the sentence.
 
• Additionally, the verb **"help" **changes to the past participle **"helped" **and the auxiliary verb **"is"/"are" **is added before it.
 
• The entity performing the action (the **"subject" **in the active sentence) is relegated to a prepositional phrase beginning with **"by".**
 
• Since **“The brave” **could refer to one individual or many individuals, the correct verb could be either **"is" **or **"are". **
 
• However, traditionally and more commonly, it's taken to mean multiple brave individuals, so **"are" **is used.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is: **"The brave are helped by God."**
 
• The structure of the passive voice sentence is: **"Object (The brave) + auxiliary verb (are) + past participle verb (helped) + by + subject (God)."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question:
Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Pick the option that gives their correct order.

A.The travel agent said that traveling by bus to the beach was the cheapest way.

B. But we went by plane because it was faster.

C. Last summer, we decided to spend our vacation at the beach. 

D. This was because the weather was very hot in the mountains.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'CDAB'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given question is an example of Sentence Jumble.
 
• The first sentence of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, statement regarding the starting of an incident or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• Sentence C should start the passage as it introduces the topic of what the subjects did for their vacation last summer. It mentions how the vacation was in the beach.
 
• Sentence D should come in the second position as it states why the subjects vacationed at the beach instead of the mountains. 
 
• Sentence A which talks about the tip given by the travel agent to go to the beach should come in the third position as it introduces the fourth sentence.
 
• Sentence B which points out the action taken by the subjects in spite of the tip given by the travel agent to access the beach rounds up the passage by coming in the fourth position. 

Thus, the sequence becomes - *Last summer, we decided to spend our vacation at the beach. This was because the weather was very hot in the mountains. The travel agent said that traveling by bus to the beach was the cheapest way. But we went by plane because it was faster. *

questions.solution: The correct answer is **'After graduating from college having a PhD degree she left the country****.'*****__Key Points__** __ • The sentence 'After graduating from college having a PhD degree she left the country' is incorrect. • The word that acts as a verb as well as an adjective, is called as a participle. • Present participle shows an action being completed in Past. • Let us explore a structure with the perfect participle (Having + V3): • Structure__: Having + V3 + Object, Subject + V2 + Object __ • Example: *Having played for so long, he rested for a while.* • *​​*Therefore, as per the rule, 'got/received' must be used after the auxiliary verb 'having.' • Therefore, the correct option is 'After graduating from college having a PhD degree she left the country.' • Correct sentence:* **After graduating from college having got/received a PhD degree she left the country.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __ • A participle phrase also acts like an adjective. • Example: *The man carrying the bricks is my father. (The participle phrase carrying the bricks* describes the *man*.)* • *​*Participles are not just used as adjectives. • They are also used to form verb tenses. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__** __ • वाक्य 'After graduating from college having a PhD degree she left the country' गलत है। • वह शब्द जो verb के साथ-साथ adjective के रूप में कार्य करता है, participle कहलाता है। • Present participle अतीत में पूर्ण की जा रही एक क्रिया को दर्शाता है। • आइए हम perfect participle (Having + V3) के साथ एक संरचना का पता लगाएं: • Structure__: Having + V3 + Object, Subject + V2 + Object • Example: *Having played for so long, he rested for a while.* • अतः नियम के अनुसार auxiliary verb 'having' के बाद 'got/received' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए। 36:Tb25, The correct answer is '**SQRP**'.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Shila enquired whether his name was Mohit.

options.text: Shila said to him, “If his name was Mohit."
Shila said to him, “Is your name Mohit?"
Shila said to him, “Who is Mohit?"
Shila said to him, “Whose name is Mohit?"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Shila said to him, “Is your name Mohit?"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in indirect speech, and we need to convert it to direct speech.
 
• When we change an indirect speech to direct speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• ​The reporting verb 'Said' is converted into 'enquired' as per the sentence's sense.
 
• The conjunction 'that' is replaced with inverted commas ("...") to show the direct speech part.
 
• A comma (,) is added after the direct speech part.
 
• The first word of the direct speech is in capital letters.
 
• The reported speech will be introduced with an auxiliary verb or 'wh'-word.
 
• Interrogative Verbs such as “ask”, “enquire”, “demand”, “want to know”, etc are used as Reporting Verbs before the Reported Speech in place of simple Verbs “say” or “tell”.
 
• “whether” is used after the Reporting Verb or object of the Reporting verb in the Indirect Narration.
 
 
 
• Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

 

Hence, direct speech is-* **Shila said to him, “Is your name Mohit?"*

questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct indirect version of the direct speech?

"I'm optimistic that despite these challenges, we're fully capable of making this project a grand success," Lucas declared at the all-hands meeting.

options.text: At the all-hands meeting, Lucas declared that he was optimistic that they were fully capable of making that project a grand success, despite those challenges.
Lucas proclaimed at the all-hands meeting that he is optimistic that despite the challenges, they are capable of making the project a grand success.
In the all-hands meeting, Lucas declared his optimism that despite these challenges, they were perfectly capable of turning this project into an immense success.
Lucas asserted in the all-hands meeting that he remained optimistic that, notwithstanding the challenges, they were fully capable of making the project a grand success.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'At the all-hands meeting, Lucas declared that he was optimistic that they were fully capable of making that project a grand success, despite those challenges.'**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence in the Direct Speech is in **Present Continuous** tense ("I'm optimistic") and in **present Simple** tense ("we're fully capable").
 
• Therefore, when converting to Indirect Speech, the Present Continuous tense should be converted into Past Continuous tense, and Present Simple tense should be converted into Past Simple tense. This aligns with the standard rule in English grammar that states we should shift the tense back one step when changing from direct to indirect speech.
 
• As per this rule: Present Continuous (Subject + is/are/am + verb + ing) in the direct speech should be converted into Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + verb + ing). And Present Simple (Subject + verb/verb+s) should be converted into Past Simple (Subject + verb in past form).
 
• Hence, "**I'm optimistic**" becomes "**he was optimistic**" and "**we're fully capable**" becomes "**they were fully capable**" in the Indirect Speech.
 
• Furthermore, the original speech's immediate or proximate spatial and temporal references need to be moved away in the indirect speech. As a result, "**this**" becomes "**that**", and "**these**" becomes "**those**".

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

 
• Option 2 incorrectly maintains present tense in the reported speech.
 
• Option 3 fails to adequately convey the original wording from the direct speech, and doesn't maintain appropriate tense consistency.
 
• Option 4 introduces the word "remained", which alters the original phrasing and meaning.
